knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 1.2.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly pairs summary tools and exploratory visualisations with variable type and analysis aim?
knowledge_checks.body: Select EDA tool choice aligned to aim.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Summaries and plots should match type and question. Mean-only, pie defaults, or skipping plots for correlations mis-serve EDA.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Match summary/plot to type and aim; means can hide shape.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Mean-only tables, pie misuse, or correlation without visual checks.

choices.label: Tool choice depends on variable type and the exploratory question: for example counts may use bar charts or histograms to reveal mass and tail behaviour; means alone can hide zero-inflation or skew.
EDA always uses the sample mean and a pie chart regardless of variable type because any numeric column is continuous.
Exploratory visualisation is optional once correlation coefficients are computed because numbers replace plots.
Pie charts are the default for any frequency exploration because they show part-to-whole structure for every count variable.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 1.2.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Claim counts per policy-year: many zeros, a long right tail of large counts. Aim: explore frequency shape before modelling. Which statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: Choose visualisation and refuse misuse for zero-inflated counts.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Zero mass and tail need shape plots. Mean-only, pie charts, or jumping to correlation without shape checks miss the stated aim.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Histogram/bar for zero and tail; refuse mean-only or pie.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Mean-only summary, pie misuse, or correlation without EDA.

choices.label: Use a bar chart or histogram of counts (or a zero-aware frequency plot) to reveal mass at zero and the right tail. Refuse a pie chart of policies or a mean-only summary that hides zero-inflation and tail behaviour.
Use the sample mean count alone because one number summarises the distribution for modelling decisions.
Use a pie chart of policy segments because part-to-whole display always shows zero-inflation clearly.
Skip visual exploration and proceed directly to correlation with premium because coefficients replace shape diagnostics.

worked_example.title: Choose summaries for zero-inflated claim counts
worked_example.problem_statement: Five policy-years show claim counts 0, 0, 1, 3, 10 (many zeros and a long right tail). Aim: explore frequency shape before modelling. Compute the mean and median, then choose an exploratory summary/plot approach that reveals zero mass and the tail.

given.note: EDA tool choice, not a full model fit

worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Compute mean and median, then decide whether mean-only summarises the shape you need to see.

steps.label: Compute mean and median
steps.attempt_cue: Average the five counts; then take the middle ordered value.
steps.explanation: Ordered counts are 0, 0, 1, 3, 10. The mean is pulled by the large count; the median sits at the middle observation.

steps.label: Choose exploratory tools for shape
steps.attempt_cue: Name a plot/summary that shows zero mass and the right tail.
steps.explanation: A bar chart or histogram of counts (or a zero-aware frequency plot) reveals mass at zero and the long tail. Mean-only hides both features.
steps.calculation: Prefer histogram/bar (zero-aware) over mean-only; median/IQR support the centre/spread story

steps.label: Refuse pie / mean-only
steps.attempt_cue: State why a pie of policies or mean-only fails the exploratory aim.
steps.explanation: A pie chart of policies does not display the count distribution's zero inflation and tail. A mean of 2.8 alone misrepresents the typical frequency shape.
steps.calculation: Refuse pie-of-policies and mean-only as shape EDA
steps.result: Mean-only / pie rejected for this aim

worked_example.final_answer: Mean = 2.8 and median = 1; use a histogram or bar chart of counts (with median/IQR support) to reveal zero mass and the right tail. Refuse mean-only or a pie chart for this exploratory aim.
worked_example.common_pitfall: Reporting only the mean count 2.8 as the exploratory summary, which hides zero-inflation and the long right tail that the modelling stage must confront.
